newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Oil prices could average around $16-$18 -- BP chief.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices could average around $16-$18 -- BP chief.

text.p: World oil prices could average between $16-$18 a barrel over the next few years and refining margins are also expected to stay weak, according to the chief executive of British Petroleum Plc.
Oil prices could stay within "a range that we think of about $16-$18 a barrel," BP's John Browne said in an interview with Reuters.
"We might look back and see the prices of last year somewhat out of line with the averages that we are seeing (now)."

Browne, who said he believed it was "foolish" to forecast oil prices, refused to give an exact time period for his projection but said "something like that" when asked if his estimate would be the average for the next three years.
World oil prices fell to six-month lows on Friday to just under $20 -- dropping by 20 percent over the last six weeks.
April crude oil futures closed Friday at $21.39 a barrel, down 30 cents on the New York Mercantile Exchange.
Browne, who sees world demand growing by 2 percent a year or two million barrels a day, said the current price "weakness is still quite high" compared with the average price over the past decade.

"There is clearly good underlying demand. Demand seems to be growing well. Last year it was growing very strongly and it started the year off well. But of course there is a lot of supply...," he said.
Browne said that 1997 refining margins were expected to stay low also due to oversupply.

"Refining margins have been very weak and again we see quite a lot of excess capacity coming on the market this year ... We believe that the refining margin will remain relatively weak this year," he said.
